\begin{abstract}
% TARGET: 150 words. Contribution sentence first, then the headline number.
% The contribution sentence this paper is built around:
%   "What a class description buys a zero-shot classifier is the vocabulary of
%    its documents, and its value is predicted by the lexical overlap between the
%    class name and those documents. Where the overlap is near zero (NACE
%    sections over German trade register text, 1.0%) definitions are worth 26.8
%    points; where it is substantial (20 Newsgroups, 18.2%) they are worth
%    nothing. Language does not matter in either setting."
% One positive claim, one mechanism, two negative controls, two datasets.
% Note what this is NOT about: keyword extraction. Three measurements give that
% half of the pipeline no credit, so do not claim it here.
FIXME
\end{abstract}

% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section{Introduction}
% TARGET: 3 paragraphs — problem, gap, contribution list.
%
% P1 Problem. Assigning economic activity codes to free-text business purposes;
%    why it matters; why labelled data is scarce.
% P2 Gap. Unsupervised keyphrase extraction ignores the target taxonomy;
%    zero-shot classification ignores the vocabulary the taxonomy carries.
% P3 Contributions, as a list:
%    (i)   class description content, not language, drives zero-shot taxonomy
%          classification: +26.8 points from label to definition, -2.3 (n.s.)
%          from translating the same content, replicated on a second encoder;
%    (ii)  a mechanism: the gain is predicted by the lexical overlap between the
%          class name and the documents, measurable before any run;
%    (iii) a replication on 20 Newsgroups where that overlap is 18x higher and
%          the same elaboration is worth nothing, as the mechanism predicts;
%    (iv)  a negative result: with informative descriptions, hand-written seed
%          keyword lists add nothing;
%    (v)   a held-out protocol for error-driven taxonomy edits, and an
%          evaluation set with a documented annotation protocol.
FIXME
